overview: The Advisory Teams for Education Planning and Site Safety reviewed design priorities for the high school project, focusing on inclusive learning environments and campus security. The teams established a framework for finalizing recommendations to the Building Committee in March 2026.

items.title: Education Planning Priorities and Project Givens
items.summary: Architects outlined core priorities for equity and inclusion, including the integration of special education into learning communities and the establishment of a 'house' model for student belonging.

items.title: Shared Classroom Model
items.summary: The team confirmed that a shared classroom model is an MSBA requirement for project efficiency and discussed the need for dedicated teacher planning spaces to support the transition.

items.title: Integrated Learning Communities
items.summary: Designers presented floor plan concepts that co-locate core academics, CTE programs, and student services to eliminate the isolation of departments.

items.title: Toilet Room Equity and Safety
items.summary: The committee discussed transitioning to more inclusive toilet models, including all-gender facilities with full-height doors to improve privacy and discourage vaping.

items.title: Wellness and Respite Spaces
items.summary: The group reviewed the need for student decompression areas and outdoor access to support mental health and staff well-being.

items.title: CTE and Performing Arts Identity
items.summary: Discussion focused on showcasing student work through transparent CTE shops, a 1,000-seat auditorium, and centralizing the 'Mustang Mall' school store.

items.title: Security and CPTED Principles
items.summary: The safety team reviewed Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) principles, including natural surveillance and the use of electronic access controls.

items.title: Mobility, Access, and Topography
items.summary: Designers presented student arrival data and addressed the challenges of making the site's steep 80-foot grade change accessible for wheelchair users and cyclists.

items.title: Athletic Facilities and Community Programs
items.summary: The group advocated for bringing football and track facilities onto the campus to eliminate transportation barriers that currently disadvantage high-needs students.

items.title: Ecology and Site Constraints
items.summary: The team examined the physical site's proximity to the Fells, existing flooding issues in the building, and the presence of significant bedrock.

items.title: Construction Logistics and Safety
items.summary: The team discussed the safety requirements for managing an active campus during phased construction, including secure fencing and temporary classroom modulars.

items.title: Project Next Steps
items.summary: Both teams scheduled meetings for March 10 and 11, 2026, to finalize design recommendations for the Building Committee using a stoplight categorization system.

items.title: Public Access to the Fells
items.summary: Members debated the security implications of non-badged members of the public using the school parking lot to access regional hiking trails.

subject: High School Design and Education Planning Priorities
